title: Sewing Machine Brands: Singer, Brother, Janome and Juki
description: Guides to the sewing machine brands you meet most in the UK: their history, what each is known for, who their machines suit and how to get parts and servicing.
intro: The history, strengths and best uses of the brands most often found in UK homes, schools and workrooms.

image.alt: Black and white photo of a sewing machine

cardText: History, strengths and who suits each brand: Singer, Brother, Janome, Juki.

sections.h2: Why brand matters less than you think
sections.html: Every major brand makes good and basic machines. What matters most is the model, its build quality, and whether a local dealer can service it. See our brand reviews for Bernina, Pfaff, Jack and Yamato too, and ask a specialist such as PK Sewing Machines which models they can support.

sections.h2: How to compare brands for your sewing
sections.html: Rather than picking by name alone, start with what you will sew: dressmaking, quilting, alterations or heavy fabrics. Then compare the features you will actually use, the availability of spare parts and presser feet, and how easy servicing is where you live. Our how to choose a sewing machine guide walks through this, and sewing machine parts covers spares.

faqs.q: Which sewing machine brand is best for beginners?
faqs.a: There is no single best brand. Look for a model with simple controls, a good stitch selection for your projects and easy access to servicing and parts. Our brand guides and the choosing guide help you narrow it down.

faqs.q: Do these brands all make industrial machines?
faqs.a: Some brands are better known for domestic machines and others for industrial work. See our industrial sewing machines page for the differences.
